description:
Собираю команду для проекта Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer — интерактивного тренажёра, в котором дети смогут попробовать себя в роли астронавтов: выполнять миссии, решать задачи и узнавать, как устроено освоение космоса.

Меня интересует, как технологии и игровая подача могут сделать обучение увлекательнее. Готов взять на себя разработку концепции, визуальную подачу и подготовку презентации проекта.

Ищу в команду:

* Разработчика — для создания рабочего прототипа

Orbit Academy is a browser-based 3D educational game developed by Team Collapsar for the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. Players arrive at a Martian outpost before its crew and restore the base with Lumi, a robot companion.

Across three chapters and twelve connected missions, players repair circuits, clean solar panels, grow food, explore with a rover and distribute limited power between life support, protection and research. Supplies and upgrades carry forward, allowing players to see how earlier decisions affect later missions.

Archived NASA CCMC DONKI solar energetic particle records provide the context for a space-weather warning. Players can inspect the original NASA records, then respond through simplified resource-management decisions. The game clearly distinguishes historical data from fictional teaching rules.

Orbit Academy makes engineering trade-offs visible through actions and consequences. It includes guided instructions, English and Russian interfaces, illustrated mission videos and local progress saving. The working prototype still requires testing with children to evaluate usability and learning outcomes.
details:
Orbit Academy is a browser-based 3D game created by Team Collapsar for the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. The player arrives at a Martian outpost before its crew and works with Lumi, a robot companion, to prepare the base.

HOW IT WORKS

The campaign contains three chapters and twelve connected missions. Players reconnect circuits, clean solar panels, restore oxygen production, plant seeds, drive a rover, collect samples and choose equipment upgrades. The final missions involve shelter supplies, repairs, antenna alignment and planning three operating shifts.

Resources, inventory and upgrades persist between missions. A battery upgrade increases the final power budget, while a greenhouse upgrade improves food production. During a warning, players must balance life support, protection and research.

NASA DATA

The game includes fourteen archived NASA CCMC DONKI solar energetic particle records from 8–14 May 2024. A 10 May event provides the context for a story warning. Players can inspect the original records and follow their NASA links.

The archive supplies historical context. Resource quantities, scanner readings, readiness scores and consequences are simplified teaching rules. The game does not calculate radiation doses on Mars or real shielding performance.

USER EXPERIENCE

A short introduction explains the goal and controls. Route guidance and contextual hints show the next action. Players can move through the outpost, open task interfaces and return to the game without losing completed actions. English is the default language for new visitors, with Russian available through a visible switch. Progress saves locally on the device.

TOOLS AND AI USE

The project uses JavaScript, Three.js, HTML and CSS. NASA records are bundled as JSON, browser localStorage stores progress, and Vercel hosts the game.

ChatGPT assisted with concept development, code, interface text and testing. AI-generated illustrations support the story. Mission videos use locally rendered animation of those illustrations. These fictional scenes are distinct from NASA data.

PURPOSE AND CURRENT STATUS

The project aims to help young learners understand engineering trade-offs through actions and visible consequences. The working prototype includes the complete campaign. Automated checks cover mission progression, resource rules, upgrade branches and invalid choices.

Testing with children is still needed to evaluate usability, engagement and learning outcomes. Performance on real mobile devices also requires further validation.
